profile.lede: I am a Computer Engineer who builds reliable software that continues to perform efficiently long after launch day.

paragraphs.t: My core focus bridges the gap between Computer Engineering and
: I design and develop backend architecture using Django and PostgreSQL, build frontend systems with React, and manage the infrastructure that keeps these systems running
The true quality of any software is proven after its release. Leveraging my engineering background, I focus on building
—maintainable, clearly structured, and engineered around real-world constraints from the very first commit.
Most of my work sits at the intersection of
, and frontend engineering—solving problems that span the entire stack from a comprehensive engineering perspective.

items.description: At Flint Consulting, I develop and maintain production-ready full-stack web applications using Django and React. My role involves designing scalable REST APIs, implementing secure authentication systems, and architecting database structures with PostgreSQL and MySQL. I also manage the Linux VPS infrastructure—configuring Nginx, Gunicorn, domain mapping, and SSL certificates—while overseeing production deployments and maintaining secure hosting environments with robust backup strategies.

During my internship as a Computer Engineer at Emara Hail, I developed a real-time data acquisition system and contributed to the design and implementation of UI/UX interfaces. I focused on troubleshooting complex issues at the intersection of hardware and software, while systematically documenting all engineering solutions and technical workflows.

I managed operational reporting and handled large-scale datasets, ensuring high levels of data integrity. By leveraging advanced Excel and Google Sheets functions, I maintained accurate figures and dependable reports to support seamless business operations.

projects.title: Projects
projects.subtitle: A deep dive into the systems I've engineered from backend architecture to live production deployments.

items.title: AARC
items.subtitle: Four role-specific workspaces operating on one recruitment and rental-management backend.

overview.t: AARC is a production-grade recruitment platform coordinating the full operational workflow across
four independent dashboards

: Employees, External Offices, Administration, and Rental Administration. A shared Django REST Framework backend centralizes authentication, records, and workflow transitions, while each React-based dashboard exposes only the specific actions and tools relevant to its role.

architecture.frontend: React dashboards featuring role-aware navigation, dynamic forms, and operational queues, connected via a unified API client
architecture.backend: Django REST Framework handling core authentication, complex permission policies, workflow endpoints, and administrative services
architecture.database: MySQL relational database optimized for user management, recruitment records, rental operations, and state tracking
architecture.deployment: Linux VPS infrastructure utilizing Nginx as a reverse proxy and Gunicorn to serve the Django application

highlights: Four tailored dashboards for Employees, External Offices, Administrators, and Rental Managers
Centralized authentication with granular, role-based authorization enforced at the API level
Automated recruitment workflows that move through controlled operational states rather than disconnected manual updates
Full production stack hosted and operated on a self-managed Linux VPS
challenges: Enabling four dashboards to share a single backend without leaking records or actions between roles
Maintaining workflow consistency when multiple teams interact with the same recruitment process
Ensuring high availability for React and Django services on a self-managed production server
solutions: Implemented reusable DRF permission policies and scoped every database query to the authenticated user's role
Modeled recruitment stages as validated backend state transitions to prevent invalid workflow actions
Orchestrated static delivery, reverse proxying, and application serving through a robust Nginx and Gunicorn configuration

items.title: Shahm Law
items.subtitle: A law-firm website backed by a custom publishing, request, and communication system.

overview.t: Shahm Law combines a professional legal-services interface with a
purpose-built Content Management System (CMS)

. The central administration dashboard manages site content, team access, newsletter subscribers, and email campaigns, alongside contact enquiries, service requests, and internal notifications within a single, organized workspace.

architecture.frontend: Public-facing service pages and a secure administration dashboard for content management and communication tracking
architecture.backend: Custom CMS and application services for structured publishing, role-based access control, newsletter management, and automated request processing
architecture.database: A relational model linking pages, subscribers, enquiries, service requests, users, and notifications for seamless data flow
architecture.deployment: Production deployment at shamlaw.sa with integrated automated email-delivery workflows

highlights: Structured content publishing allowing editors to update the site without code modifications
End-to-end management of newsletter subscriptions and outbound campaigns within the admin system
Streamlined operational queues that separate general enquiries from specific legal service requests
Granular role management limiting publishing and communication capabilities to authorized personnel
challenges: Combining editorial workflows and client-service operations without creating a cluttered dashboard
Managing large-scale newsletter delivery while preventing duplicate campaigns
Keeping public forms accessible while protecting sensitive administrative workflows
solutions: Separated content, subscribers, and requests into focused modules sharing a unified access model
Built campaign and recipient state-tracking into the workflow to ensure reliable and verifiable delivery
Validated public submissions through dedicated endpoints and exposed them only to authorized roles

items.title: KneeGuide
items.subtitle: A connected rehabilitation prototype that turns Arduino knee-angle readings into clinical exercise records.

overview.t: KneeGuide connects a specialized React healthcare interface to an Arduino-based measurement device via Bluetooth. During assigned exercises, the platform captures
real-time knee-angle measurements
, providing immediate visual feedback to the patient while storing session results for doctors to analyze through detailed reports, progress tracking, and exercise management tools.

architecture.frontend: React dashboards for both doctors and patients, featuring Bluetooth pairing, live angle visualization, and progress reporting
architecture.backend: Django services managing user accounts, clinical relationships, exercise protocols, appointments, and measurement sessions
architecture.database: A robust relational model managing patient/doctor data, assignments, sessions, and granular angle observations
architecture.deployment: Research web prototype hosted at knee.fyaa.io, integrated with an Arduino Bluetooth measurement unit

highlights: Dedicated doctor workspace for prescribing exercises and reviewing session-level analytics
Patient workspace for managing appointments, routines, and guided device-assisted measurements
Real-time visualization that converts hardware sensor data into actionable feedback during movement
Digital progress tracking that compares completed sessions with numerical precision, replacing manual logs
challenges: Maintaining a stable Bluetooth connection and preventing data loss during signal drops
Synchronizing high-frequency real-time measurements with the correct patient and session context
Presenting complex movement data clearly without overwhelming the user with raw sensor samples
solutions: Engineered a robust pairing lifecycle with connection state validation and automated recovery handling
Normalized angle observations at the software level before linking them to active exercise sessions for data integrity
Separated live feedback visualization from summarized analytical reports while preserving detailed readings for further research

items.title: TripSplit
items.subtitle: A shared trip ledger for joining groups, recording expenses, and tracking the remaining budget.

overview.t: TripSplit provides travel groups with a single, unified financial record. A trip owner creates the workspace and distributes a simple
invite code
; members join the same ledger to record expenses and view real-time updates on spending and the remaining budget, eliminating the need for separate or manual calculations.

architecture.frontend: A responsive web interface for trip creation, code-based joining, member management, and real-time budget summaries
architecture.backend: Application services that enforce trip membership, validate invite codes, manage expense ownership, and perform accurate budget calculations
architecture.database: A relational ledger connecting trips, members, invite codes, and expense entries to ensure data synchronization across all users

highlights: Short invite codes allowing travelers to join the correct trip seamlessly without manual coordination
Every recorded expense is linked to the shared trip and the specific member who entered it for full transparency
Real-time remaining budget derived from a single authoritative ledger visible to all members
Membership management for trip owners while participants maintain the ability to record costs
challenges: Preventing invite codes from granting unauthorized access to unrelated trips
Keeping financial totals consistent when multiple members add or revise expenses simultaneously
Representing membership and expense ownership without duplicating trip data per user
solutions: Implemented server-side validation and resolution of codes before establishing scoped membership
Derived budget summaries from authoritative database records rather than relying on client-side calculations
Modeled trips, memberships, and expenses as separate entities so a single ledger serves every participant efficiently

items.title: Dorina Pro
items.subtitle: A browser-based football tournament engine for league and knockout competitions.

overview.t: Dorina Pro manages football tournaments entirely in the browser. Organizers choose league or knockout mode, enter teams and results, and the application derives
standings, qualifiers, winners, and the final top three
from tournament state persisted in LocalStorage.

architecture.frontend: Single-page tournament interface with separate league and knockout calculation flows
architecture.backend: None; tournament rules and progression are executed in the browser
architecture.database: LocalStorage persistence for teams, fixtures, results, standings, and tournament progress

highlights: League tables recalculate points and ordering as match results change
Knockout rounds advance winners automatically through the bracket
Tournament state survives refreshes without accounts or a remote database
Completion logic announces the champion and final top-three positions
challenges: Supporting league and knockout rules without mixing incompatible progression models
Reconstructing a valid tournament after a browser refresh
Handling edited results without leaving standings or winners stale
solutions: Isolated each competition mode behind deterministic calculation functions
Serialized minimal tournament state and recomputed derived views when loading
Made standings and advancement derived data so edits trigger a consistent recalculation

items.title: Student Results
items.subtitle: A lightweight result lookup that reads synchronized student records directly from Google Sheets.

overview.t: Student Results replaces a custom application server with
Google Sheets as the maintained data source
. Staff continue updating familiar spreadsheets while students search the synchronized records through a focused frontend using their identifying information.

architecture.frontend: Search interface that validates student input, queries the published dataset, and presents the matching result
architecture.backend: No custom backend; Google Sheets provides the managed record source
architecture.database: Google Sheets rows containing synchronized student result records

highlights: Staff update results through their existing spreadsheet workflow
The frontend reads synchronized records without a separately maintained API server
Student-information search narrows access to the requested record
The small deployment surface keeps operational overhead low
challenges: Using a spreadsheet as a live source while keeping lookup behavior predictable
Normalizing cells with inconsistent spacing, casing, or number formatting
Avoiding unnecessary infrastructure for a narrowly scoped read-only workflow
solutions: Added normalization before comparing search fields with sheet values
Kept the flow read-only and treated the spreadsheet as the single maintained source
Used a static client architecture independent of a custom application server

items.title: Terhal
items.subtitle: A bilingual, multi-page website for presenting a non-profit organization’s work and programs.

overview.t: Terhal is a React website spanning more than ten Arabic and English pages. It organizes the organization’s identity, programs, and public information into a shared
bilingual page system
that adapts navigation, reading direction, and responsive layouts across both languages.

architecture.frontend: React component system shared across more than ten Arabic and English pages
architecture.backend: None; public information is delivered as a frontend-only website
architecture.database: None; page content is bundled with the site
architecture.deployment: Static deployment on Netlify at terhalv1.netlify.app

highlights: More than ten pages share consistent navigation and reusable sections
Arabic layouts switch reading direction without maintaining a separate site
Both languages preserve the same information hierarchy
Responsive behavior covers dense internal pages and the landing experience
challenges: Keeping navigation and structure synchronized across two languages and many routes
Supporting RTL and LTR without duplicating every component
Maintaining readable hierarchy across mobile and desktop breakpoints
solutions: Centralized route and navigation definitions for both languages
Built shared React sections with direction-aware layout rules
Defined responsive behavior at component level for consistency across long-form pages

items.title: OQOL
items.subtitle: A tailored WordPress implementation that gives the client direct control over routine content updates.

overview.t: OQOL is a WordPress implementation customized around the client’s page and publishing requirements. WordPress acts as the operational content layer so the team can
maintain pages without developer intervention
while the public presentation remains constrained to the approved structure.

architecture.frontend: Customized WordPress theme and page templates aligned with the client’s content structure
architecture.backend: WordPress administration with configured editing controls and media management
architecture.database: WordPress relational content store for pages, settings, and media references

highlights: Templates reflect required content types instead of exposing a blank page builder
Routine copy and media changes are handled through WordPress administration
Reusable content patterns keep repeated sections consistent
The implementation stays within familiar WordPress operations for handover
challenges: Adapting editing flexibility to a fixed client-approved presentation
Preventing routine content changes from breaking page structure
Keeping administration simple for editors who do not work with code
solutions: Mapped recurring content into constrained templates and reusable fields
Limited editing choices to the controls needed for each page type
Configured the CMS around the client’s publishing workflow

items.title: CodeDuo
items.subtitle: A corporate services website that turns software capabilities into a clear enquiry path.

overview.t: CodeDuo presents software-development services through a responsive corporate frontend. The information architecture moves from capability areas to service detail and contact actions using
consistent branded components
rather than unrelated landing-page sections.

architecture.frontend: Responsive component-based website for service pages, company information, and enquiry paths
architecture.backend: No application backend required for the public presentation layer
architecture.database: None; corporate content is delivered with the frontend

highlights: Service categories are structured around specific software-delivery capabilities
Repeated patterns create continuity between overview and service detail
Contact actions remain accessible across desktop and mobile layouts
Typography, spacing, and color rules are reusable frontend primitives
challenges: Explaining several technical service lines without creating a dense catalogue
Maintaining one visual system across differently sized sections
Preserving clear enquiry paths on small screens
solutions: Grouped offerings by client problem and delivery outcome
Created shared section, typography, and spacing primitives
Placed responsive contact actions at deliberate decision points

items.title: Social
items.subtitle: An open-source, bilingual link hub designed for self-hosting and custom identity.

overview.t: Social is a self-hostable alternative to hosted link-in-bio services. It packages profile details, destinations, bilingual content, and visual identity into a
small deployable frontend
that can be branded and published without depending on a subscription platform.

architecture.frontend: Responsive bilingual link page with configurable profile, destinations, and branding
architecture.backend: None required for the core project
architecture.database: Configuration-based content; no database service required
architecture.deployment: Static, self-hostable build with a live instance at social.fyaa.io

highlights: Arabic and English profiles are delivered from one lightweight codebase
Brand colors, identity, and destination links can be replaced without rebuilding the layout
No third-party link-platform account is required
Static output deploys to simple hosting with minimal operational cost
challenges: Keeping customization approachable without a full administration backend
Making the compact layout work naturally in RTL and LTR
Keeping the page fast when opened from mobile social applications
solutions: Separated profile content and brand settings from presentation components
Used direction-aware rules so one component tree supports both languages
Avoided server-side dependencies to keep deployment small
